source.author: cic
source.text: Si nihil existimat contra naturam fieri hominibus violandis, quid cum eo disseras, qui omnino hominem ex homine tollat?
source.text_original: Si nihil existimat contra naturam fieri hominibus violandis, quid cum eo disseras, qui omnino hominem ex homine tollat?
source.text_english: If he thinks that nothing is done contrary to nature by violating human beings, what argument can you have with someone who altogether removes man from man?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: hoc est enim hominem ex homine tollere et in corpore constitutum esse sine corpore et optare potius quam docere dicente apostolo: miser ego homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius?
reuse.text_original: hoc est enim hominem ex homine tollere et in corpore constitutum esse sine corpore et optare potius quam docere dicente apostolo: miser ego homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius?
reuse.text_english: For this is to take a man away from man and, while he is established in the body, to be without a body, and to prefer wishing rather than teaching, while the Apostle says: Wretched man that I am, who will deliver me from the body of this death?
